source: Human NimA-related kinases (Neks) have multiple mitotic and non-mitotic functions, but few substrates are known.

claim: The phosphorylation-site motifs for the entire Nek kinase family, except for Nek11, were systematically determined.
source: We systematically determined the phosphorylation-site motifs for the entire Nek kinase family, except for Nek11.

claim: All Nek kinases strongly select for hydrophobic residues in the −3 position.
source: While all Nek kinases strongly select for hydrophobic residues in the −3 position, the family separates into four distinct groups based on specificity for a serine versus threonine phospho-acceptor, and preference for basic or acidic residues in other positions.

claim: The Nek kinase family separates into four distinct groups based on specificity for a serine versus threonine phospho-acceptor, and preference for basic or acidic residues in other positions.

claim: Nek10 is a dual-specificity kinase that efficiently phosphorylates itself and peptide substrates on serine and tyrosine.

claim: Nek10 activity is enhanced by tyrosine auto-phosphorylation.
source: Unlike Nek1-Nek9, Nek10 is a dual-specificity kinase that efficiently phosphorylates itself and peptide substrates on serine and tyrosine, and its activity is enhanced by tyrosine auto-phosphorylation.
evidence: This is supported by data showing that the Y644F mutation dramatically reduced Nek10 activity (Figure 5G).

claim: Nek10 dual-specificity depends on residues in the HRD+2 and APE-4 positions that are uncommon in either serine/threonine or tyrosine kinases.

claim: The phosphorylation-site motifs for the mitotic kinases Nek6, Nek7 and Nek9 are essentially identical to that of their upstream activator Plk1.

claim: Nek1/3/4/5/8 preferentially phosphorylate threonine residues.
source: Most notably, our results revealed a dichotomy in phospho-acceptor site preference within the family, with Nek1/3/4/5/8 preferentially phosphorylating threonine residues, while Nek6/7/9 primarily targeted peptides with serine residues as the phospho-acceptor (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is shown in the OPLS data in Figure 1C.

claim: Nek6/7/9 primarily target peptides with serine residues as the phospho-acceptor.
source: Most notably, our results revealed a dichotomy in phospho-acceptor site preference within the family, with Nek1/3/4/5/8 preferentially phosphorylating threonine residues, while Nek6/7/9 primarily targeted peptides with serine residues as the phospho-acceptor (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is shown in the OPLS data in Figure 1C.

claim: Nek2 preferentially phosphorylates serine residues as the phospho-acceptor.
source: Nek2 phosphorylated the serine phospho-acceptor library more efficiently than the threonine library, indicating that Nek2 shares a preference for a phospho-acceptor serine residue with Nek6/7/9 (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is shown in the in vitro kinase assay data in Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: The Nek kinase family has a core consensus motif of [LMFW]-X-X-S/T-[no P].

claim: Nek1/3/4/5/8 display a preference for hydrophobic and basic residues on multiple positions within the motif.
source: In general, Nek1/3/4/5/8 displayed a preference for hydrophobic and basic residues on multiple positions within the motif, while Nek6/7/9 displayed a preference for acidic residues and selected hydrophobic residues at various positions.

claim: Nek6/7/9 display a preference for acidic residues and selected hydrophobic residues at various positions.

evidence: This is shown in the in vitro kinase assay data in Figure 2B,C.

claim: Nek3 is substantially impaired in its ability to phosphorylate peptides in which either the −3 or −2 hydrophobic residues are mutated to aspartic acid.
source: As shown in Figure 2B,C, Nek3 could readily phosphorylate the optimal Nek13458-tide but was substantially impaired in its ability to phosphorylate peptides in which either the −3 or −2 hydrophobic residues were mutated to aspartic acid (Figure 2B,C).
evidence: This is shown in the in vitro kinase assay data in Figure 2B,C.

claim: Nek7 phosphorylates the optimal 679-tide much more rapidly than a 679-tide variant containing a disfavored hydrophobic residue (I) in place of the favored hydrophobic residue (L) in the −3 position.
source: As shown in Figure 2D, Nek7 phosphorylated the optimal 679-tide much more rapidly than a 679-tide variant containing a disfavored hydrophobic residue (I) in place of the favored hydrophobic residue (L) in the −3 position (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is shown in the in vitro kinase assay data in Figure 2D.

claim: Substitution of the favored aspartic acid residue in the −2 position for a basic residue (R) substantially reduces peptide phosphorylation by Nek7.
source: Similarly, substitution of the favored aspartic acid residue in the −2 position for a basic residue (R), substantially reduced peptide phosphorylation by Nek7 (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is shown in the in vitro kinase assay data in Figure 2D.

claim: Nek6 and Nek7 show a clear preference for substrate peptides that are already phosphorylated on tyrosine on the −1 position.
source: In addition to the four specificity-groups, we identified amino acid selection preferences that are unique to individual Nek kinases. evidence: This is shown in the OPLS data and validated by peptide phosphorylation assays in Figure 2E.

claim: The preference of Nek6 and Nek7 for phospho-tyrosine in the −1 position suggests cross-talk between tyrosine and serine/threonine kinases during mitosis.
source: In addition to the four specificity-groups, we identified amino acid selection preferences that are unique to individual Nek kinases. For example, Nek6 and Nek7 showed a clear preference for substrate peptides that are already phosphorylated on tyrosine on the −1 position, suggesting cross-talk between tyrosine and serine/threonine kinases during mitosis.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on the observed preference for pY in the −1 position.

claim: Tyrosine phosphorylation events play a role in mitotic signaling.
source: It is becoming increasingly clear that tyrosine phosphorylation events do, in fact, play a role in mitotic signaling (Caron et al., 2016), and multiple tyrosine kinases have been shown to prefer an acidic residue in the −1 position (Miller and Turk, 2018), which would generate good target sites for Nek6/7 (i.e. a DE-pY-S motif).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Caron et al., 2016.

claim: Multiple tyrosine kinases prefer an acidic residue in the −1 position.
source: It is becoming increasingly clear that tyrosine phosphorylation events do, in fact, play a role in mitotic signaling (Caron et al., 2016), and multiple tyrosine kinases have been shown to prefer an acidic residue in the −1 position (Miller and Turk, 2018), which would generate good target sites for Nek6/7 (i.e. a DE-pY-S motif).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Miller and Turk, 2018.

claim: Substitution of the phospho-tyrosine in the −1 position of 679-tide to an isoleucine residue reduces the rate at which Nek6 phosphorylates 679-tide.
source: To validate this specificity, we substituted the phospho-tyrosine in the −1 position of 679-tide to an OPLS-disfavored isoleucine residue, which resulted in a reduced rate at which Nek6 phosphorylated 679-tide (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is shown in the in vitro kinase assay data in Figure 2E.

claim: All Nek kinases display a strong preference for a tryptophan in the −4 position.
source: Finally, all the Nek kinases displayed a strong preference for a tryptophan in the −4 position.
evidence: This is shown in the OPLS data in Figure 1C.

claim: Selection for tryptophan within kinase substrate motifs, especially at the −4 position, has rarely been observed.
source: Selection for tryptophan within kinase substrate motifs, especially at the −4 position, has rarely been observed (Miller and Turk, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Miller and Turk, 2018.

claim: The rate at which Nek8 phosphorylates its optimal substrate Nek8-tide is reduced upon substitution of the tryptophan in the −4 position to a valine.
source: Corroborating our OPLS-data, the rate at which Nek8 phosphorylated its optimal substrate Nek8-tide was reduced upon substitution of the tryptophan in the −4 position to a valine (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is shown in the in vitro kinase assay data in Figure 2F.

claim: Introduction of a tryptophan in the −4 position in a peptide that is otherwise a very poor substrate for Nek8 significantly enhances the rate at which Nek8 can phosphorylate the peptide.
source: Furthermore, introduction of a tryptophan in the −4 position in a peptide that is otherwise a very poor substrate for Nek8 (Nek8-poor) significantly enhanced the rate at which Nek8 could phosphorylate Nek8-poor (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is shown in the in vitro kinase assay data in Figure 2F.

claim: Nek10 displays very little sequence preference for any residue, except for a tyrosine at every position in OPLS experiments with serine/threonine peptide libraries.
source: Curiously, in these OPLS experiments, Nek10 displayed very little sequence preference for any residue, except for a tyrosine at every position (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is shown in the OPLS data in Figure 3A.

claim: Mass spectrometry analysis of in vitro auto-phosphorylated Nek10 revealed the presence of several phosphorylated tyrosine residues.
source: In agreement with this hypothesis, a preliminary, non-comprehensive mass spectrometric experiment to analyse phospho-sites on in vitro auto-phosphorylated Nek10 revealed the presence of several phosphorylated tyrosine residues (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is shown in the mass spectrometry data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: Nek10 effectively phosphorylates peptides with a serine phospho-acceptor site.
source: Surprisingly, Nek10 effectively phosphorylated peptides with a serine phospho-acceptor site, but even more rapidly phosphorylated peptides with a tyrosine phospho-acceptor site (Figure 3B,C).
evidence: This is shown in the in vitro kinase assay data in Figure 3B,C.

claim: Nek10 more rapidly phosphorylates peptides with a tyrosine phospho-acceptor site than peptides with a serine phospho-acceptor site.
source: Surprisingly, Nek10 effectively phosphorylated peptides with a serine phospho-acceptor site, but even more rapidly phosphorylated peptides with a tyrosine phospho-acceptor site (Figure 3B,C).
evidence: This is shown in the in vitro kinase assay data in Figure 3B,C.

claim: Substitution of threonine as the phospho-acceptor significantly impairs peptide phosphorylation by Nek10.
source: In contrast, substitution of threonine as the phospho-acceptor significantly impaired peptide phosphorylation by Nek10 (Figure 3B,C).
evidence: This is shown in the in vitro kinase assay data in Figure 3B,C.

claim: Nek10 has an isoleucine in the APE-4 position whereas all the other Nek kinases have a proline at this position.
source: We therefore aligned the P+1 loop sequences of the Nek kinase family members, and noted that Nek10 has an isoleucine whereas all the other Nek kinases have a proline at the position four residues N-terminal of the APE-motif (APE-4; Figure 3E).
evidence: This is shown in the sequence alignment in Figure 3E.

claim: An isoleucine in the APE-4 position is typically found in tyrosine kinases, but in less than 5% of serine/threonine kinases.
source: Interestingly, an isoleucine in the APE-4 is typically found in tyrosine kinases, but in less than 5% of serine/threonine kinase, which more commonly have a proline on this position (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is shown in the frequency analysis in Figure 3F.

claim: Mutation of the APE-4 isoleucine in Nek10 to a proline (I693P) increases its capacity to phosphorylate a substrate peptide on a serine residue but renders Nek10 incapable of phosphorylating the same peptide on a tyrosine.
source: We therefore mutated the APE-4 isoleucine in Nek10 to a proline (I693P) and found that this increased its capacity to phosphorylate a substrate peptide on a serine residue but rendered Nek10 incapable of phosphorylating the same peptide on a tyrosine (Figure 3G).
evidence: This is shown in the in vitro kinase assay data in Figure 3G.

claim: Nek10 has a threonine in the HRD+2 position, which is uncommon within the serine/threonine kinome.
source: Intriguingly, Nek10 has a threonine in the HRD+2 position, which is uncommon within the serine/threonine kinome.
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in the sequence alignment in Figure 3H.

claim: 86% of serine/threonine kinases contain a lysine residue in the HRD+2 position.
source: Instead, 86% of serine/threonine kinases contain a lysine residue in the HRD+2 position, including all the other Nek kinases (Figure 3H; Figure 3—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is shown in the frequency analysis in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Mutation of the HRD+2 threonine to a lysine (T657K) generates a Nek10 variant that can effectively phosphorylate serine residues but is incapable of phosphorylating tyrosine residues.
source: Mutation of the HRD+2 threonine to a lysine (T657K) generated a Nek10 variant that, like Nek10 I693P, could effectively phosphorylate serine residues but was incapable of phosphorylating tyrosine residues (Figure 3I).
evidence: This is shown in the in vitro kinase assay data in Figure 3I.

claim: The Nek10 T692P variant can detectably phosphorylate tyrosine residues while it is unable to phosphorylate serine residues.
source: However, the resulting Nek10 T692P variant could still detectably phosphorylate tyrosine residues while it was unable to phosphorylate serine residues (Figure 3K).
evidence: This is shown in the in vitro kinase assay data in Figure 3K.

claim: Point-mutations in the catalytic or P+1 loop can toggle Nek10 between being a dual-specificity, serine-specific, or tyrosine-specific kinase.
source: Taken together, these results identify specific residues in the kinase domain of Nek10 that are essential for its dual-specificity, and show that point-mutations in the catalytic or P+1 loop can toggle Nek10 between being a dual-specificity, serine-specific, or tyrosine-specific kinase.
evidence: This is inferred from the mutagenesis experiments showing that different mutations alter phospho-acceptor specificity (Figure 3G,I,K).

claim: Murine Nek1 has been reported to be a dual-specificity kinase.
source: However, murine Nek1 has been reported to be a dual-specificity kinase (Letwin et al., 1992), suggesting that Nek1 might have intrinsic tyrosine-phosphorylation capacity in specific contexts, and might therefore be more susceptible than other serine/threonine kinases to mutations that broaden phospho-acceptor specificity.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Letwin et al., 1992.

claim: The Nek1 APE-4 isoleucine mutant enhances the relative preference of Nek1 for tyrosine substrates to ~20% of the efficiency with which it phosphorylates threonine-containing peptides.
source: Nonetheless, the APE-4 isoleucine mutant, but not the HRD+2 threonine mutant, enhanced the relative preference of Nek1 for tyrosine substrates (Figure 3—figure supplement 3E) to ~ 20% of the efficiency with which it phosphorylated threonine-containing peptides.
evidence: This is shown in the in vitro kinase assay data in Figure 3—figure supplement 3E.

claim: Nek10 phosphorylates tyrosine substrates with at least twofold greater activity than the same peptide on a serine or threonine phosphoacceptor.
source: Nek10, however, in contrast to the Nek1 APE-4 isoleucine mutant, phosphorylates tyrosine substrates with at least twofold greater activity than the same peptide on a serine or threonine phosphoacceptor (Figure 3C), indicating that additional sequence determinants in the Nek10 kinase domain must collaborate with the APE-4 isoleucine residue to enhance dual-specificity.
evidence: This is shown in the in vitro kinase assay data in Figure 3C.

claim: Additional sequence determinants in the Nek10 kinase domain must collaborate with the APE-4 isoleucine residue to enhance dual-specificity.
source: Nek10, however, in contrast to the Nek1 APE-4 isoleucine mutant, phosphorylates tyrosine substrates with at least twofold greater activity than the same peptide on a serine or threonine phosphoacceptor (Figure 3C), indicating that additional sequence determinants in the Nek10 kinase domain must collaborate with the APE-4 isoleucine residue to enhance dual-specificity.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of Nek10 and Nek1 APE-4 mutant activities.

claim: The positioning of the substrate in the catalytic site of the kinase is different for serine/threonine kinases compared to tyrosine kinases.
source: The positioning of the substrate in the catalytic site of the kinase is different for serine/threonine kinases compared to tyrosine kinases (Taylor et al., 1995), raising the question of how a dual-specificity kinase is able to correctly position substrates to catalyze phosphorylation on serine as well as tyrosine residues.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Taylor et al., 1995.

claim: Nek10 I693P displays a clear preference for hydrophobic and basic residues, similar to the Nek1/3/4/5/8 group.
source: As shown in Figure 4A, for Nek10 I693P the strong preference for tyrosine in every position was absent, but instead it displayed a clear preference for hydrophobic and basic residues, similar to the Nek1/3/4/5/8 group (Figures 1C, 4A).
evidence: This is shown in the OPLS data in Figure 4A.

claim: Nek10 I693P preferentially phosphorylates serine as the phospho-acceptor.
source: However, in contrast to other members of this group that preferentially select for threonine as the phospho-acceptor, Nek10 I693P preferentially phosphorylates serine (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is shown in the OPLS data in Figure 4A.

claim: WT Nek10 can effectively phosphorylate (S)-tide but not the −3D and −1D peptides.
source: As shown in Figure 4B, WT Nek10 could effectively phosphorylate (S)-tide but not the −3D and −1D peptides, therefore corroborating our OPLS-results (Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is shown in the in vitro kinase assay data in Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The tyrosine phosphorylation-site motif of Nek10 is substantially more restricted than the serine phosphorylation-site motif.
source: Thus, the serine phosphorylation-site motif of the dual-specificity kinase Nek10 is similar to that of the other Nek kinases, but the tyrosine phosphorylation-site motif of Nek10 is substantially more restricted.
evidence: This is inferred from comparison of OPLS data for Nek10 on serine versus tyrosine peptide libraries (Figure 4A,C).

claim: On tyrosine substrates, Nek10 shows a near-absolute requirement for aromatic or selected hydrophobic residues in the +1 position.
source: On tyrosine substrates, Nek10 does not select for the canonical Nek-family motif signature [LMFW]-X-X-S/T-[no P], but instead shows a near-absolute requirement for aromatic or selected hydrophobic residues in the +1 position (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is shown in the OPLS data in Figure 4C.

claim: Nek10 can undergo auto-phosphorylation on both serine and tyrosine residues in vitro.
source: Indeed, incubation of Nek10 with radiolabeled ATP revealed efficient auto-phosphorylation of WT and serine-specific Nek10 (I693P(Ser)), but not of kinase-dead (KD) Nek10 in which the catalytic aspartic acid was mutated to an asparagine residue (Figure 5A). Furthermore, despite its reduced activity, we could also clearly detect auto-phosphorylation of the tyrosine-specific (T692P(Tyr)) Nek10 variant, demonstrating that Nek10 can undergo auto-phosphorylation on both serine and tyrosine residues in vitro (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is shown in the auto-phosphorylation assay data in Figure 5A.

claim: Nek10 can auto-phosphorylate in trans on both serine and tyrosine residues in vitro.
source: As shown in Figure 5B, phosphorylation of KD Nek10 was observed following incubation with either a serine-specific or tyrosine-specific kinase-proficient Nek10, demonstrating that in vitro, Nek10 can auto-phosphorylate in trans on both serine and tyrosine residues (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is shown in the trans-phosphorylation assay data in Figure 5B.

claim: GSK-3 and DYRK kinases can auto-phosphorylate on tyrosine residues, but do this exclusively (GSK3) or primarily (DYRK) during folding in cis.
source: Members of the GSK3 and DYRK serine/threonine kinase families can also auto-phosphorylate on tyrosine residues, but do this exclusively (GSK3) or primarily (DYRK) during folding in cis (Cole et al., 2004; Soundararajan et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Cole et al., 2004 and Soundararajan et al., 2013.

claim: Clear tyrosine phosphorylation was observed of WT Nek10, but not of a KD or serine-specific variant, consistent with Nek10 auto-phosphorylation on tyrosine residues in cells.
source: Clear tyrosine phosphorylation was observed of WT Nek10, but not of a KD or serine-specific variant, consistent with Nek10 auto-phosphorylation on tyrosine residues in cells (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is shown in the immunoblotting data in Figure 5D.

claim: Y644 is a major auto-phosphorylation target site of Nek10.
source: As shown in Figure 5E, tyrosine-phosphorylation was detected on each of the mutants, but the signal was substantially reduced upon mutation of Y644 (Figure 5E). A possible interpretation of these results is that Y644 is a major auto-phosphorylation target site of Nek10.
evidence: This is inferred from the reduced tyrosine phosphorylation signal in the Y644F mutant (Figure 5E) and confirmed by trans-phosphorylation assays (Figure 5F).

claim: Nek10 directly auto-phosphorylates Y644 in trans in vitro.
source: To test this hypothesis, we performed an in vitro kinase assay using an active tyrosine-specific form of Nek10 to phosphorylate in trans either a KD Nek10 Y644 control, or a KD Nek10 containing the Y644F mutation (Figure 5F). This experiment confirmed that in vitro, Nek10 directly auto-phosphorylates Y644 in trans (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is shown in the trans-phosphorylation assay data in Figure 5F.

claim: The Y644F mutation dramatically reduces the activity of Nek10.
source: Interestingly, the Y644F mutation dramatically reduced the activity of Nek10 in an in vitro kinase assay with a serine peptide substrate (Figure 5G), and a similar result was obtained with a tyrosine peptide substrate (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is shown in the in vitro kinase assay data in Figure 5G and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Nek10 auto-phosphorylation on Y644 contributes to its activity.
source: These results strongly indicate that Nek10 auto-phosphorylation on Y644 contributes to its activity.
evidence: This is inferred from the dramatic reduction in activity of the Y644F mutant (Figure 5G).

claim: S358 of Nek10 is an auto-phosphorylation target site.
source: To determine which of these four sites was the most likely target site, we manually annotated the MS/MS spectra, and identified S358 of Nek10 as the phosphosite most consistent with the mass spectrometry data (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is shown in the mass spectrometry data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C,E and validated by trans-phosphorylation assays in Figure 5H.

claim: Nek10 can auto-phosphorylate both in vitro and in cells.
source: Therefore, we conclude from these results that Nek10 can auto-phosphorylate both in vitro and in cells, that in vitro auto-phosphorylation can occur in trans, and we identified Y644 in the kinase domain, and S358 outside of the kinase domain, as auto-phosphorylation target sites.
evidence: This is supported by multiple experiments showing auto-phosphorylation in vitro (Figure 5A,B) and in cells (Figure 5D).

claim: In vitro auto-phosphorylation of Nek10 can occur in trans.
source: Therefore, we conclude from these results that Nek10 can auto-phosphorylate both in vitro and in cells, that in vitro auto-phosphorylation can occur in trans, and we identified Y644 in the kinase domain, and S358 outside of the kinase domain, as auto-phosphorylation target sites.
evidence: This is shown in the trans-phosphorylation assay data in Figure 5B,F,H.

claim: Y644 in the kinase domain is an auto-phosphorylation target site of Nek10.
source: Therefore, we conclude from these results that Nek10 can auto-phosphorylate both in vitro and in cells, that in vitro auto-phosphorylation can occur in trans, and we identified Y644 in the kinase domain, and S358 outside of the kinase domain, as auto-phosphorylation target sites.
evidence: This is shown in multiple experiments including Figure 5E,F,G.

claim: S358 outside of the kinase domain is an auto-phosphorylation target site of Nek10.
source: Therefore, we conclude from these results that Nek10 can auto-phosphorylate both in vitro and in cells, that in vitro auto-phosphorylation can occur in trans, and we identified Y644 in the kinase domain, and S358 outside of the kinase domain, as auto-phosphorylation target sites.
evidence: This is shown in the mass spectrometry data (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C,E) and trans-phosphorylation assays (Figure 5H).

claim: Hierarchical clustering based on quantitative OPLS motif information reveals that Nek1/3/4/5/8 are clearly separated from Nek2/6/7/9/10(S).
source: This clustering revealed that Nek1/3/4/5/8 were clearly separated from Nek2/6/7/9/10(S) (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is shown in the hierarchical clustering analysis in Figure 6A.

claim: The division of the Nek kinases based on preferred substrate sequence cannot be explained by amino acid sequence similarity between the Nek kinase domains themselves.
source: Importantly, this division of the Nek kinases based on preferred substrate sequence cannot be explained by amino acid sequence similarity between the Nek kinase domains themselves (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is shown by comparing the clustering based on motif specificity (Figure 6A) with clustering based on kinase domain sequence identity (Figure 6B).

claim: An important contributor to the hierarchy of Nek kinases is the preference for either serine or threonine as the phospho-acceptor site.
source: Instead, an important contributor to this hierarchy is the preference for either serine or threonine as the phospho-acceptor site (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is shown in the heatmap in Figure 6C.

claim: Within the group of threonine-directed Nek kinases, Nek 1/3/4 cluster separately from Nek 5/8.
source: This revealed that within the group of threonine-directed Nek kinases, Nek 1/3/4 cluster separately from Nek 5/8 (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is shown in the hierarchical clustering analysis excluding phospho-acceptor site preference in Figure 6D.

claim: The Nek kinase family can be separated into four specificity groups based on phospho-acceptor preference and additional amino acids specificities.
source: Overall then, the motif data indicate that the Nek kinase family can be separated into four specificity groups based on phospho-acceptor preference and additional amino acids specificities (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is shown in the hierarchical clustering analysis in Figure 6D and summarized in Figure 7A.

claim: Nek 1, 3 and 4 cluster in Group 1 based on their shared preference for arginine in the −1 position.
source: Interpretation of the sequence logos shown in Figure 1C indicates that Nek 1, 3 and 4 cluster in Group 1 based on their shared preference for arginine in the −1 position.
evidence: This is inferred from the OPLS data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Nek 1 and 4 show strong selectivity for lysine and arginine in the +2 position.
source: Within Group 1, Nek 1 and 4 also show strong selectivity for lysine and arginine in the +2 position, and they are exceptional in their lack of preference for a tryptophan in the −3 position.
evidence: This is inferred from the OPLS data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Nek 1 and 4 are exceptional in their lack of preference for a tryptophan in the −3 position.
source: Within Group 1, Nek 1 and 4 also show strong selectivity for lysine and arginine in the +2 position, and they are exceptional in their lack of preference for a tryptophan in the −3 position.
evidence: This is inferred from the OPLS data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Group 2 consists of Nek 5 and 8.
source: Group 2 consists of Nek 5 and 8, and is closely related to Group 1, but has a less prominent selection for arginine in the −1 position.
evidence: This is shown in the hierarchical clustering in Figure 6D and the motif data in Figure 1C.

claim: Group 3 consists of Nek 2 and 10.
source: Group 3, which consists of Nek 2 and 10, are distinguished by their serine phospho-acceptor specificity (Figure 6C; Figure 3—figure supplement 2A), although the remaining motif specificity of Nek two is similar to that of kinases in Group 2 (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is shown in the hierarchical clustering in Figure 6D and the motif data.

claim: Group 4 consists of Nek 6, 7, and 9.
source: Finally, Group 4 consists of Nek 6, 7, and 9, and clusters distantly from the rest (Figure 6D) based on a preference for acidic residues in the −5,–4, and particularly in the −2 position that is not shared with any of the other Nek kinases (Figure 6E; Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is shown in the hierarchical clustering in Figure 6D and the motif data in Figure 6E.

claim: Group 4 Nek kinases have a preference for acidic residues in the −5, −4, and particularly in the −2 position that is not shared with any of the other Nek kinases.
source: Finally, Group 4 consists of Nek 6, 7, and 9, and clusters distantly from the rest (Figure 6D) based on a preference for acidic residues in the −5,–4, and particularly in the −2 position that is not shared with any of the other Nek kinases (Figure 6E; Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is shown in the heatmaps in Figure 6E and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Nek7 has two basic regions that are absent from Nek1, which might accommodate acidic residues N-terminal of the phospho-acceptor site.
source: To rationalize the unusual selectivity for acidic residues displayed by Group 4 Nek kinases, we compared the X-ray crystal structures of the Nek1 and Nek7 kinase domains (Haq et al., 2015; Melo-Hanchuk et al., 2017). This revealed the presence of two basic regions in Nek7 that are absent from Nek1, and might accommodate acidic residues N-terminal of the phospho-acceptor site (Figure 6F).
evidence: This is shown in the structural comparison in Figure 6F and supported by citations to Haq et al., 2015 and Melo-Hanchuk et al., 2017.

claim: 13458-tide is a considerably better substrate for Nek3 than 679-tide.
source: As predicted, 13458-tide was a considerably better substrate for Nek3 than 679-tide, and this was reversed for Nek7 (Figure 6G).
evidence: This is shown in the in vitro kinase assay data in Figure 6G.

claim: 679-tide is a considerably better substrate for Nek7 than 13458-tide.
source: As predicted, 13458-tide was a considerably better substrate for Nek3 than 679-tide, and this was reversed for Nek7 (Figure 6G).
evidence: This is shown in the in vitro kinase assay data in Figure 6G.

claim: There is a striking resemblance between the Nek6/7/9 motif and the phosphorylation-site motif previously obtained for Plk1.
source: We noticed a striking resemblance between the Nek6/7/9 motif, and the phosphorylation-site motif previously obtained for Plk1 (Figure 7A; Alexander et al., 2011).
evidence: This is shown in the motif comparison in Figure 7A and supported by citation to Alexander et al., 2011.

claim: Plk1 could not be detected in any of the isolated Nek kinase preparations.
source: To further address this potential concern, we analyzed the isolated Nek kinase preparations for co-purified Plk1 by immunoblotting (Figure 7—figure supplement 1). We could readily detect Plk1 in HEK 293T cell lysates, but could not detect Plk1 in any of the isolated Nek kinase preparations.
evidence: This is shown in the immunoblotting data in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: With regard to substrate specificity, Nek6/7/9 are more related to Plk1 than they are to the other Nek kinases.
source: We further analyzed the resemblance between the Nek6/7/9 and Plk1 motifs by hierarchical clustering of the Nek-family and Plk1 based on substrate motif data from OPLS. This revealed that, with regard to substrate specificity, Nek6/7/9 are more related to Plk1 than they are to the other Nek kinases (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is shown in the hierarchical clustering analysis in Figure 7B.

claim: Plk1 has previously been reported as the upstream activator of Nek6/7/9.
source: Importantly Plk1, together with Cdk1, has previously been reported as the upstream activator of Nek6/7/9 (Bertran et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Bertran et al., 2011.

claim: Plk1 and Nek6/7/9 not only operate together in a linear signaling cascade during mitosis, but also share the same phosphorylation-site motif.
source: Hence, Plk1 and Nek6/7/9 not only operate together in a linear signaling cascade during mitosis, but also share the same phosphorylation-site motif, and hence could potentially phosphorylate a common set of substrates.
evidence: This is inferred from the motif similarity (Figure 7A,B) and the known signaling relationship.

claim: Over 50% of Plk1 target sites are also predicted to be a good target site for at least one of the Nek kinases.
source: This analysis revealed a substantial overlap in candidate substrates among the different kinases: over 50% of Plk1 target sites were also predicted to be a good target site for at least one of the Nek kinases, and a total of 2801 sites were predicted to be good target sites for all four kinases (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is shown in the Venn diagram analysis in Figure 7C based on Scansite scoring.

claim: A total of 2801 sites are predicted to be good target sites for all four kinases (Plk1, Nek6, Nek7, and Nek9).
source: This analysis revealed a substantial overlap in candidate substrates among the different kinases: over 50% of Plk1 target sites were also predicted to be a good target site for at least one of the Nek kinases, and a total of 2801 sites were predicted to be good target sites for all four kinases (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is shown in the Venn diagram analysis in Figure 7C based on Scansite scoring.

claim: There is a strong correlation between the Nek7-scores and Plk1-scores for candidate Plk1 substrates at the mitotic spindle.
source: Scansite scoring of these substrates showed a strong correlation between the Nek7-scores and Plk1-scores (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is shown in the scatter plot in Figure 7D.

claim: 109 distinct sites on 77 different proteins are potential targets of both Plk1 and Nek7.
source: Using a cut-off for the top 25% of best-scoring sites, we identified 109 distinct sites on 77 different proteins as potential targets of both Plk1 and Nek7.
evidence: This is based on Scansite scoring analysis of candidate Plk1 substrates from Santamaria et al., 2011.

claim: S453 on Cdc27 has been established as a direct Plk1 substrate.
source: This included S453 on Cdc27, and S170 on RacGAP1, both of which have been established as direct Plk1 substrates (Kraft et al., 2003; Burkard et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Kraft et al., 2003 and Burkard et al., 2009.

claim: S170 on RacGAP1 has been established as a direct Plk1 substrate.
source: This included S453 on Cdc27, and S170 on RacGAP1, both of which have been established as direct Plk1 substrates (Kraft et al., 2003; Burkard et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Kraft et al., 2003 and Burkard et al., 2009.

claim: Cdc27 is readily phosphorylated by WT but not KD Plk1.
source: As previously reported, Cdc27 was readily phosphorylated by WT but not KD Plk1, and this phosphorylation was reduced by mutation of the S434/S435 target site (Figure 7E, upper panels; Kraft et al., 2003).
evidence: This is shown in the in vitro kinase assay data in Figure 7E and supported by citation to Kraft et al., 2003.

claim: Phosphorylation of Cdc27 by Plk1 is reduced by mutation of the S434/S435 target site.
source: As previously reported, Cdc27 was readily phosphorylated by WT but not KD Plk1, and this phosphorylation was reduced by mutation of the S434/S435 target site (Figure 7E, upper panels; Kraft et al., 2003).
evidence: This is shown in the in vitro kinase assay data in Figure 7E and supported by citation to Kraft et al., 2003.

claim: Nek7 can phosphorylate Cdc27 on the same site as Plk1.
source: Interestingly, the same assay performed with Nek7 instead of Plk1 demonstrated that Nek7 could also phosphorylate Cdc27 on the same site as Plk1 (Figure 7E, lower panels).
evidence: This is shown in the in vitro kinase assay data in Figure 7E.

claim: RacGAP1 is directly phosphorylated by both Plk1 and Nek7.
source: A second in vitro kinase assay using RacGAP1 confirmed that this substrate is also directly phosphorylated by both Plk1 and Nek7, although phosphorylation was not reduced by mutation of S170, indicating that both kinases appear to target sites other than or in addition to S170 (Figure 7F).
evidence: This is shown in the in vitro kinase assay data in Figure 7F.

claim: Plk1 and Nek6/7/9 share a strikingly similar phosphorylation-site motif.
source: Together, these experiments indicate that Plk1 and Nek6/7/9 share a strikingly similar phosphorylation-site motif, have substantial overlap in potential substrates in the phosphoproteome, and are capable of phosphorylating the same protein substrates on the same target sites in vitro.
evidence: This is supported by the motif comparison (Figure 7A,B) and in vitro kinase assays (Figure 7E,F).

claim: Plk1 and Nek6/7/9 have substantial overlap in potential substrates in the phosphoproteome.
source: Together, these experiments indicate that Plk1 and Nek6/7/9 share a strikingly similar phosphorylation-site motif, have substantial overlap in potential substrates in the phosphoproteome, and are capable of phosphorylating the same protein substrates on the same target sites in vitro.
evidence: This is supported by the Scansite analysis (Figure 7C,D).

claim: Plk1 and Nek6/7/9 are capable of phosphorylating the same protein substrates on the same target sites in vitro.
source: Together, these experiments indicate that Plk1 and Nek6/7/9 share a strikingly similar phosphorylation-site motif, have substantial overlap in potential substrates in the phosphoproteome, and are capable of phosphorylating the same protein substrates on the same target sites in vitro.
evidence: This is shown in the in vitro kinase assays with Cdc27 and RacGAP1 (Figure 7E,F).

claim: A strong determinant of phospho-acceptor site specificity is the residue in the activation loop of the kinase at the DFG+1 position.
source: A strong determinant of phospho-acceptor site specificity is the residue in the activation loop of the kinase at the DFG+1 position (Chen et al., 2014), and the observed dichotomy of serine versus threonine phospho-acceptor preference within the Nek family can be explained by the presence of a leucine versus isoleucine/serine in this position (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Chen et al., 2014 and shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The observed dichotomy of serine versus threonine phospho-acceptor preference within the Nek family can be explained by the presence of a leucine versus isoleucine/serine in the DFG+1 position.
source: A strong determinant of phospho-acceptor site specificity is the residue in the activation loop of the kinase at the DFG+1 position (Chen et al., 2014), and the observed dichotomy of serine versus threonine phospho-acceptor preference within the Nek family can be explained by the presence of a leucine versus isoleucine/serine in this position (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is inferred from the correlation between DFG+1 residue identity and phospho-acceptor preference shown in Figure 6C.

claim: All kinases in specificity Groups 3 (Nek2/10) and 4 (Nek6/7/9) have been implicated in one or more mitotic processes, with the exception of Nek10.
source: To date, all kinases in specificity Groups 3 (Nek2/10) and 4 (Nek6/7/9) have been implicated in one or more mitotic processes, with the exception of Nek10.
evidence: This is stated based on the literature review in the introduction.

claim: Nek10 has previously been reported to play a role in the response to UV-stress.
source: The exact function of Nek10 is not known, but it has previously been reported to play a role in the response to UV-stress (Moniz et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Moniz et al., 2011.

claim: The Nek kinase specificity clustering might reflect functional divergence between mitotic and non-mitotic Nek kinases.
source: It is therefore tempting to speculate that the Nek kinase specificity clustering might reflect functional divergence between mitotic and non-mitotic Nek kinases.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on the observed clustering and known functions.

claim: Good substrates for a kinase usually contain phosphorylation site sequences that closely match the optimal sequence motif for the kinase.
source: In general, good substrates for a kinase usually contain phosphorylation site sequences that closely match the optimal sequence motif for the kinase, although additional factors including secondary docking sites, surface accessibility, and substrate protein conformation also play important roles (Linding et al., 2007; Miller and Turk, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Linding et al., 2007 and Miller and Turk, 2018.

claim: Additional factors including secondary docking sites, surface accessibility, and substrate protein conformation play important roles in substrate recognition.
source: In general, good substrates for a kinase usually contain phosphorylation site sequences that closely match the optimal sequence motif for the kinase, although additional factors including secondary docking sites, surface accessibility, and substrate protein conformation also play important roles (Linding et al., 2007; Miller and Turk, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Linding et al., 2007 and Miller and Turk, 2018.

claim: Too few substrates have been definitively and reproducibly characterized for most of the individual Nek kinases to allow quantitative comparison of those sites with the optimal motifs.
source: However, to date, too few substrates have been definitively and reproducibly characterized for most of the individual Nek kinases to allow quantitative comparison of those sites with the optimal motifs.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation in the current knowledge.

claim: The maximal number of substrates reported for any Nek kinase is eleven (for Nek6).
source: The maximal number of substrates reported for any Nek kinase is eleven (for Nek6), with less than five substrates known for all other Nek kinases except for Nek2.
evidence: This is stated based on literature review.

claim: There are no published substrates for Nek 4, 5, 8, and 10.
source: There are no published substrates for Nek 4, 5, 8, and 10.
evidence: This is stated based on literature review.

claim: A global analysis of all previously reported Nek kinase target sites reveals an overrepresentation of leucine and phenylalanine in the −3 position.
source: Nonetheless, a global analysis of all previously reported Nek kinase target sites (Supplementary file 1) reveals an overrepresentation of leucine and phenylalanine in the −3 position, consistent with the motif reported here.
evidence: This is based on analysis of previously reported substrates in Supplementary file 1.

claim: Of the eleven published Nek6 substrates, three contain an asparagine on the −2 position.
source: Of the eleven published Nek6 substrates, three contain an asparagine on the −2 position, which we identified as a specificity unique to Group 4 Nek kinases, and four others have a glycine, which is also positively selected for by Nek6.
evidence: This is based on analysis of previously reported substrates.

claim: Substrate phosphorylation by a kinase does not require a perfect match between the target site and the optimal motif.
source: However, it is important to emphasize that substrate phosphorylation by a kinase does not require a perfect match between the target site and the optimal motif. Rather, the better the site matches the optimal motif, the more efficiently it is phosphorylated by the kinase (Obenauer et al., 2003), as we also demonstrate here in our peptide phosphorylation studies (Figure 2B-F).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Obenauer et al., 2003 and demonstrated in Figure 2B-F.

claim: The better the site matches the optimal motif, the more efficiently it is phosphorylated by the kinase.
source: However, it is important to emphasize that substrate phosphorylation by a kinase does not require a perfect match between the target site and the optimal motif. Rather, the better the site matches the optimal motif, the more efficiently it is phosphorylated by the kinase (Obenauer et al., 2003), as we also demonstrate here in our peptide phosphorylation studies (Figure 2B-F).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Obenauer et al., 2003 and demonstrated in Figure 2B-F.

claim: Nek10 joins a small group of human serine/threonine kinases with reported dual-specificity.
source: Importantly, our assays revealed that Nek10 is a dual-specificity kinase, and thus joins a small group of human serine/threonine kinases with reported dual-specificity.
evidence: This is based on the experimental data showing Nek10 can phosphorylate both serine and tyrosine residues.

claim: The small group of human serine/threonine kinases with reported dual-specificity includes GSK-3 kinases, DYRK-kinases, MAP2K-family kinases, TTK, CK2, Myt1 and TESK-kinases.
source: These are the GSK-3 kinases, the DYRK-kinases, the kinases of the MAP2K-family, TTK, CK2, Myt1 and the TESK-kinases (Gómez and Cohen, 1991; Lindberg et al., 1993; Wang et al., 1994; Kentrup et al., 1996; Liu et al., 1997; Wilson et al., 1997; Toshima et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: GSK-3 only phosphorylates tyrosine residues when auto-phosphorylating during folding in cis.
source: GSK-3 and the DYRK kinases only phosphorylate tyrosine residues when auto-phosphorylating during folding in cis, although it was recently reported that the folded, mature DYRK1A retains a weak tyrosine auto-phosphorylation capability (Cole et al., 2004; Lochhead et al., 2005; Soundararajan et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Cole et al., 2004; Lochhead et al., 2005; Soundararajan et al., 2013.

claim: The folded, mature DYRK1A retains a weak tyrosine auto-phosphorylation capability.
source: GSK-3 and the DYRK kinases only phosphorylate tyrosine residues when auto-phosphorylating during folding in cis, although it was recently reported that the folded, mature DYRK1A retains a weak tyrosine auto-phosphorylation capability (Cole et al., 2004; Lochhead et al., 2005; Soundararajan et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Cole et al., 2004; Lochhead et al., 2005; Soundararajan et al., 2013.

claim: TTK and CK2 have weak tyrosine phosphorylation activity compared to their serine phosphorylation activity.
source: TTK and CK2 have weak tyrosine phosphorylation activity compared to their serine phosphorylation activity, and Myt1 and the kinases of the MAP2K family only phosphorylate on tyrosine and threonine in the very distinct context of a TY-site on Cdk1 and a TxY-site on MAP kinases, respectively (Gómez and Cohen, 1991; Lindberg et al., 1993; Liu et al., 1997; Marin et al., 1999).
